rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Repeating the object pronoun gives worship and fear exclusive force and focus that omitting its repetition would lack.
rows.anchor: ففي إعادة الضمير من قوة الاقتضاء لذلك ما ليس في حذفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the object of seeking aid unstated makes the request cover every worldly and otherworldly need, not only worship or obedience.
rows.anchor: أراد إطلاق الاستعانة لتشمل كل شيء يريده الإنسان

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: The omitted object gives seeking aid general scope; otherwise the verse would leave aid for needs beyond worship unknown.
rows.anchor: في سر إطلاق الاستعانة فقيل: ليتناول كلَّ مُستعانٍ فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verbs signal Islam’s communal character, reflected in congregational prayer, mosques, pilgrimage, charity, jihad, shared fasting and feasts, and visiting the sick.
rows.anchor: وذلك إشارة إلى أهمية الجماعة في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recurring plural prayer in every rakʿah reinforces collective worship; congregational prayer is worth twenty-seven times individual prayer.
rows.anchor: وهذه السورة التي تتردد في كل ركعة من ركعات الصلاة فيها إشارة إلى أهمية الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam’s communal practices include pilgrimage, social solidarity through alms, collective jihad, and fasting and feast days binding the Muslim community.
rows.anchor: والحج أكبر مظهر جماعي، والزكاة والصدقات من أكبر مظاهر التكافل الاجتماعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural form of worship and seeking aid extends the supplication beyond the speaker to all believers, as the author’s cited views explain.
rows.anchor: بكلمة نعبد ونستعين واهدنا

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The plural nūn encourages a person to perform prayer in congregation.
rows.anchor: إن المراد من هذه النون نون الجمع، وهو تنبيه على أن الأولى

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Because believers are siblings, saying we worship includes all believers across the world and seeks the Muslims’ common good.
rows.anchor: كان قد ذكر عبادة نفسه وعبادة جميع المؤمنين، شرقاً وغرباً، فكأنه سعى

rows.speaker: فتح القدير
rows.claim: The plural verbs let the supplicant speak for himself and the wider class of worshippers.
rows.anchor: والمجيء بالنون في الفعلين لقصد الإخبار من الداعي عن نفسه، وعن جنسه من العباد.

rows.speaker: فتح القدير
rows.claim: Another view takes the plural as humility: the individual is too small for this great occasion, rather than as self-exaltation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المقام لما كان عظيماً لم يستقلّ به الواحد استقصاراً لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is impossible without God’s aid and enabling; seeking aid admits human inability and dependence, countering pride and arrogance.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيع أن يقوم بعباة الله إلا بإعانة الله وتوفيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing joins what servants offer God in worship with what they need and ask from Him.
rows.anchor: وليجمع بين ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم وبين ما يطلبونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship precedes seeking aid because worship is the purpose for which humans and jinn were created, while aid is its means.
rows.anchor: العبادة هي علة خلق الإنس والجن

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Since worship is unavoidably obligatory for servants, it is more deserving of precedence than seeking aid.
rows.anchor: إن العبادة واجبة حتماً لا مناص للعباد من الإتيان بها

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Putting worship before seeking aid follows the rule that ends precede means: worship is the end and aid its instrument.
rows.anchor: إن تقديم العبادة على الاستعانة في الفاتحة من باب تقديم الغايات على الوسائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is God’s due, whereas seeking aid is the servant’s request; offering submission first is fitting before asking for something.
rows.anchor: أن العبادة قَسْمُ الربِّ وحَقُّه، وأن الاستعانة مرادُ العبد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s right in worship takes precedence over the servant’s share in seeking aid.
rows.anchor: العبادة حقُّ الله وقسمه والاستعانةُ قسمُ العبد، وحقُّ الله أولى بالتقديم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship suits mention of recompense, while seeking aid fits the ensuing request for guidance; each expression is placed beside what suits it.
rows.anchor: ومنها: أنَّ العبادة أكثرُ مناسبةً للجزاء أعني

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: Worship is more apt beside the mention of recompense, and seeking aid joins more closely to the request for guidance.
rows.anchor: أشد مناسبة بذكر الجزاء، والاستعانة أقوى التئاماً بطلب الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship relates to God’s divinity and name Allah, while seeking aid relates to His lordship and the name Rabb, matching the opening order.
rows.anchor: {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ} متعلقٌ بألوهيته واسمه (الله)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship belongs to the God-praising half of the surah, whereas the servant’s request for aid belongs with the supplication beginning guide us.
rows.anchor: فكان مع الشطر الذي له وهو {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} إلى آخر السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordering parallels the command to worship God and then rely on Him.
rows.anchor: وهذا التعبير هو نظير قوله تعالى: {فاعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delaying the seeking-aid clause also matches the surah’s verse endings.
rows.anchor: في تأخير فعل الاستعانة توافقاً مع خواتيم الآي في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from speaking about God to addressing Him is iltifāt, a rhetorical turn between grammatical perspectives.
rows.anchor: هذا يسمى التفاتاً في علم البلاغة، والالتفاتُ قد يكون عدولاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A change of style refreshes the listener and awakens attention.
rows.anchor: أن الكلام إذا نُقِلَ من أسلوب إلى أسلوب كان ذلك أحسن تطرية لنشاط السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After naming the One worthy of praise and describing His great attributes, direct address makes the exclusive worship and aid owed to Him more vivid.
rows.anchor: فقيل: إياك يا مَنْ هذه صفاته نخص بالعبادة والاستعانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Rabb of all worlds establishes His presence everywhere and always, so addressing Him as present is apt.
rows.anchor: لما وُصِفَ بأنه رب العالمين عُلِمَ أنه حاضرٌ في كل مكان وزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing someone just described in the third person can express a tactful intimacy more strongly than saying of him, I seek him.
rows.anchor: فتقول له: إياك أقصد، فيكون في هذا الخطاب من التلطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address prepares for the supplication that follows in guide us.
rows.anchor: ذكر توطئةً للدعاء في قوله: اهدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A request made to someone present is stronger than one made about someone absent.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الطلب من الحاضر أقوى من الطلب من الغائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening praise is fittingly in the third person, while supplication from this point onward is fittingly direct address.
rows.anchor: الكلام من أول السورة إلى هنا ثناءٌ، والثناء في الغيبة أَوْلى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Praise is fuller in the absent form, but worship is due to the ever-present God; hence praise uses third person and worship direct address.
rows.anchor: كانت العبادة إنما يستحقها الحاضر الذي لا يغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance can mean directing, showing, clarifying, or inspiring; the verb appears with a direct object, with ilā, or with li.
rows.anchor: معنى الهداية الإرشاد والدلالة والتبيين والإلهام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A preposition is used when the person is outside the path and must be led to it; a direct object works both for those on the path and those not yet on it.
rows.anchor: إن الفرق بين التعدية بالحرف والتعدية من دون حرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s father and the hypocrites are outside the path, while the messengers and Muhammad are already walking it, showing direct-object guidance can describe either case.
rows.anchor: فتعديةُ الفعل بنفسه تقال لمن كان فيه أي في الصراط ولمن لم يكن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance with ilā or li is used for someone not yet on the route, as in requests to be guided to the middle path or to truth.
rows.anchor: أما التعدية باللام وإلى فتكون لمن لم يكن فيه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: With a direct object, guide us includes inspire us, enable us, provide for us, or grant us; showing the two ways means explaining good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقد تُعدَّى الهداية بنفسها كما هنا: {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} فتضمن معنى ألهمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance with ilā means directing and showing the way, whereas guidance with li can mean granting success and making someone fit for it.
rows.anchor: وذلك بمعنى الإرشاد والدلالة وكذلك قوله

rows.speaker: اللسان
rows.claim: Hijazi usage takes a direct object to mean acquainting someone with the road; other dialects use ilā, as al-Akhfash reported.
rows.anchor: هديته الطريق والبيت هداية، أي: عَرَّفته، لغة أهل الحجاز

rows.speaker: ابن بري
rows.claim: He distinguishes introducing someone to the road by direct object from guiding or directing them to it with a preposition.
rows.anchor: قال ابن بري: يقال: هديته الطريق بمعنى عرّفته

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: He glosses the Quranic phrase with guide them as make it clear to them.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: أَوَ لم يُبَيِّنْ لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance has stages: one far from the way needs to be led to it, while one who has arrived needs its conditions, stages, dangers, and safe passages explained.
rows.anchor: فالبعيدُ الضالُّ عن الطريق، يحتاج إلى هادٍ يدلّه على الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can mark a purpose or endpoint; with guidance it can mean bringing a traveler to the goal that made the journey worthwhile.
rows.anchor: وقد تستعمل اللام مع الهداية لبيان الغاية من الحدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People need every kind of guidance: being returned to the route, taught its way, kept moving, and finally brought to their destination.
rows.anchor: والإنسان محتاج إلى هذه الهدايات كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Paradise describe their final arrival as God guiding them to this, the culmination of guidance.
rows.anchor: وهي خاتمة الهدايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran does not use guide with lām for a path or way because a path is a means to the goal, not the goal itself.
rows.anchor: ولذا لم نجد استعمال (هدى) مُعَدَّى باللام في القرآن الكريم مع السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith, truth, what is most upright, light, and Paradise are desired endpoints, which explains Quranic use of lām with guidance for them.
rows.anchor: فالإيمان والحق والتي هي أقوم والنورُ والجنة، كلها غاياتٌ مُرادةٌ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance with lām to an endpoint is attributed only to God or His Book; people may guide others by direct object or with ilā.
rows.anchor: اختصها الله لنفسه أو لقرآنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although a passage pairs direct-object guidance with guidance using ilā, that apparent interchange needs explanation rather than proving identical meanings.
rows.anchor: وقد تقول: لكن القرآن استعمل تعبيرين أحياناً في سياق واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired wording in the passage about paths of peace and a straight path can appear to make direct-object guidance and guidance with ilā synonymous.
rows.anchor: مما يدل على أنهما بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about guidance to truth and for truth likewise appears to treat ilā and lām as equivalent.
rows.anchor: فعداه مرة بإلى ومرة باللام فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that these constructions mean the same thing and explains the first passage by the recipients’ different starting states.
rows.anchor: والحق أنها ليست بمعنى واحد، وأن هناك ما يقتضي هذا الاختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those already following God’s pleasure need the way explained, while people in darkness need to be brought out and delivered to the straight path.
rows.anchor: فإن الذي اتَّبعَ رضوانَ الله ليس ضالاً ولا مبتعداً عن الصراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot even point to truth because they do not know where it is; God explains the way and brings seekers to their destination.
rows.anchor: وأما شركاؤهم فلا يدرون الحق أين هو؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct-object form in guide us covers both people already on the straight path, who need it explained, and believers who strayed, who need return.
rows.anchor: فهنا نطلب الهداية لمن كان في الطريق فيعرّفه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers also ask to remain firm and increase in guidance, since they need God’s support at every moment.
rows.anchor: طلب استمرار الهداية على الطريق المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God to show the true route, restore the speaker if he strays, keep him firm, and increase his guidance.
rows.anchor: عرّفنا الطريقَ الحق وردّنا إليه ردّاً جميلاً إذا ما ضللنا

rows.speaker: البحر المحيط
rows.claim: Since the worshipper has already praised God and declared worship and reliance, guide us asks for guidance to continue.
rows.anchor: ومضمون هذه الجملة طلب استمرار الهداية إلى طريق مَنْ أنعم الله عليهم

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: One interpretation asks to be kept firm in religion against doubts, supported by a Quranic prayer and a prophetic supplication for steadfast hearts.
rows.anchor: أحدها: أن معناه ثَبِّتنا على الدين كيلا تزلزلنا الشُّبَه

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: A second interpretation asks God to increase the guidance already received.
rows.anchor: وثانيها: أعطنا زيادة الهدى

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: A third interpretation takes guidance here to mean reward.
rows.anchor: وثالثها: أن الهداية الثواب

rows.speaker: روح المعاني
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation asks God to show the truth in the future as He showed it previously.
rows.anchor: ورابعها: أن المراد دُلَّنا على الحق في مستقبل عمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting us before the verb would wrongly imply that the supplicant asks for guidance only for his group and not for anyone else.
rows.anchor: لا يصلح طلب التخصيص بالهداية دون سائر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guide us matches we worship and we seek aid: once the speaker includes companions in worship, he asks guidance for all, needed to reach their aim.
rows.anchor: لأنه لما أخبر المتكلم أنه هو ومن معه يعبدون الله ويستعينونه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Invoking the congregation’s mercy, the worshipper praises, worships, seeks help, asks guidance, follows the righteous, and flees the rejected as a group.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسولك يقول: (الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب) فلما أردت تحميدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prayer made broadly for others as well as oneself is more likely to be answered.
rows.anchor: أن الدعاء كلما كان أعم كان إلى الإجابة أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praying for everyone trains a Muslim to want others to receive what he wants and counters selfishness and exclusive desire for good.
rows.anchor: أن تحب للآخرين ما تحب لنفسك فيغسل ما في النفس من درن الأثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural prayer spreads a communal spirit among individuals.
rows.anchor: إشاعة الروح الجماعية بين الأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Traveling the path together strengthens and comforts believers; solitude brings fear and fatigue, while the flock separated from the group is vulnerable.
rows.anchor: أن الاجتماع على الهدى، تثبيتٌ وقوة، وأن كثرة السائرين على الطريق تورث الأُنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request connects with Rabb of all worlds because a nurturer’s first task is to guide.
rows.anchor: لأن من معاني الرب المربي، وأول مهامّ المربي هي الهداية كما ذكرنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guiding someone is an act of mercy, so the prayer asks the Most Merciful not to abandon the supplicant to error.
rows.anchor: لأن مَنْ هداه الله فقد رحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking aid includes asking God for guidance and steadfastness on it.
rows.anchor: ومن الاستعانة أن تطلب منه الهداية والثبات عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessed are those who have followed the straight path, while those astray are lost from it; the Quran often pairs guidance and misguidance as opposites.
rows.anchor: والهدى ضد الضلال، وكثيراً ما يجمع القرآن بين الهدى والضلال على أنهما متضادان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads ṣirāṭ as a form suggesting inclusion and breadth, unlike ṭarīq and sabīl, which he derives from a beaten or heavily trodden way.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن (صراط) على وزن (فِعال) من (صراط) وهو من الأوزان الدالة على الاشتمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the form of ṣirāṭ suggests it can embrace every traveler, while ṭarīq may be narrow and fail to encompass them.
rows.anchor: فيشتمل على كل السالكين، ولا يضيق بهم فهو واسع رَحْبٌ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular, definite, annexed, and qualified straight path is one unique route, as there is only one straight line between two points.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء بالصراط مفرداً مُعَرَّفاً بتعريفين: بالألف واللام والإضافة، وموصوفاً بالاستقامة مما يدل على أنه صراط واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is Islam, the shortest and easiest route to the goal; other routes bend and fail to arrive.
rows.anchor: فالصراط المستقيم هو طريق الإسلام وهو دين الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the path aims at reaching God, meaning attaining His approval, since all people eventually return to Him.
rows.anchor: إن المراد من السلوك على الصراط، هو الوصول إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The straight line is the shortest between two points, so it suits a weak servant seeking the nearest, shortest route.
rows.anchor: الأول: أنه أقرب الخطوط وأقصرها، وأنا عاجز فلا يليق بضعفي

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Because there is only one straight path and crooked paths resemble one another, the straight way is less confusing and safer.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أن المستقيم واحد وما عداه معوجة، وبعضها يشبه بعضاً في الاعوجاج

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: A straight path reaches the destination, whereas a crooked one does not.
rows.anchor: الثالث: الطريق المستقيم يوصل إلى المقصود، والمعوج لا يوصل إليه.

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The straight route remains unchanged, unlike a crooked one.
rows.anchor: الرابع: المستقيم لا يتغير، والمعوج يتغير

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: The path’s two forms of definiteness identify one exclusive route to God, conveyed through His messengers and revealed books.
rows.anchor: وذكر الصراط المستقيم منفرداً مُعَرَّفاً بتعريفين

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: The rebellious routes are described in plural, while the way to God is one; all other approaches are closed.
rows.anchor: فوحَّد لفظ الصراط وسبيله وجمع السبل المخالفة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran uses ṣirāṭ only in the singular, unlike sabīl, because ṣirāṭ is the broad route into which the many paths lead.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن لم يأت بكلمة الصراط، إلا مُفْرَدَةً فلم يستعملها مجموعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next phrase identifies the straight path as the way of the blessed, excluding the angry and the astray and encompassing every accountable person.
rows.anchor: ثم زاد هذا الصراط بياناً وتوضيحاً، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are either blessed, or wretched in two ways: knowing truth but violating it, or lacking knowledge of truth and being astray.
rows.anchor: فهم إما أهل السعادة، وهم الذين أنعم الله عليهم.

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: One proposed reading identifies the angry as sinners and the astray as those ignorant of God.
rows.anchor: ويتجه أن يقال: المغضوب عليهم: العصاة، والضالين: الجاهلون بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No accountable person falls outside these categories: the blessed know and obey, while the wretched are sinners or ignorant.
rows.anchor: ولا يخرج أصناف المكلفين عن هؤلاء

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi classifies accountable people as obedient, sinful, or ignorant of religion and unbelieving, corresponding to the three Quranic groups.
rows.anchor: دلت هذه الآية على أن المكلفين ثلاث فرق

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Complete blessing combines knowing truth and acting on it; lacking action makes one sinful and angry upon, while lacking knowledge makes one astray.
rows.anchor: أن الذين كملت نِعَمُ الله عليهم، هم الذين جمعوا بين معرفة الحق لذاته

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: People divide by knowledge and practice: the knowledgeable doer is blessed, the knowledgeable follower of desire is angry upon, and the ignorant is astray; the first is more deserving of anger.
rows.anchor: فالعالم بالحق العامل به هو المنعم عليه

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Corrupt knowledge produces misguidance and corrupt intention produces anger; these are the two root diseases of the heart.
rows.anchor: فإن مدار اعتلال القلوب وأسقامها على أصلين: فساد العلم وفساد القصد

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Living out worship and seeking aid in knowledge, action, and inward state cures corruption of the heart and intention.
rows.anchor: والتحقق بـ {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} علماً ومعرفة وعملاً وحالاً يتضمنُ الشفاءَ

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Exclusive worship is the remedy for ostentation, and seeking aid from God is the remedy for pride and vanity.
rows.anchor: فدواء الرياء بـ {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ} ودواء الكبر بـ {وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ}

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Asking for the straight path cures ignorance; healing these spiritual diseases makes a person among the blessed, unlike those corrupt in intention or knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن مرض الجهل بـ {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} عُوفيَ من أمراضه وأسقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense in You blessed identifies established recipients, including prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people.
rows.anchor: المقصود صراط الذين ثبت إنعام الله عليهم وتحقق وهم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using a past verb for the blessed, then nominal forms for the angry and astray, distinguishes established past beneficiaries from the enduring qualities of the latter groups.
rows.anchor: فعبر عن المنعم عليهم بالفعل الماضي، ثم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A present-tense blessing would omit the earlier prophets and righteous, imply no established past recipients, and obscure continuity in one path from Adam onward.
rows.anchor: لأغفلَ كُلَّ مَنْ مضى من رسل الله والصالحين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense allows the community of the blessed to grow as each present recipient joins those already blessed; the present tense could imply only a small current group.
rows.anchor: لأن الحاضر يلتحق بالماضي، وهكذا تتسع دائرة المنعَم عليهم بمرور الزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun forms angry upon and astray cover all times and make those conditions enduring.
rows.anchor: بالاسم، فليشمل سائر الأزمنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them the blessed ones would not name the benefactor; the greatness of a gift and the honor it confers depend on who bestowed it.
rows.anchor: لم يبيّن المُنعِم الذي أنعم عليهم، والنعمة إنما تقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing blessing to the greatest giver magnifies both the gift and the recipient’s honor, as a ruler’s favor exceeds a lesser official’s.
rows.anchor: فإن كان المنعِم عظيماً عَظُمتْ نعمتهُ، وإن كان أدنى من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God attributes good and favor to Himself but leaves evil’s agent unmentioned, as in the saying that all good is in God’s hands and evil is not from Him.
rows.anchor: فنسب النعمة إلى نفسه ولم ينسب إلى نفسه الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All blessing truly comes from God, so the Quran attributes the act of bestowing blessing to Him.
rows.anchor: ولذلك ينسب النعم كلها إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sole Quranic attribution of blessing to someone besides God occurs when the Prophet’s special favor to Zayd is mentioned after God’s favor to him.
rows.anchor: ولم يسند فعل النعمة إلى غير الله، إلا في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive angry upon leaves the agent broad, including God and those angry for Him; even former allies disown and curse the condemned in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فقد بناه للمفعول ليعم الغضب عليهم: غضب الله، وغضب الغاضبين لله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The passive avoids attributing anger directly to the God being addressed in a humble request for favor and also prepares the ending’s parallelism and rhyme.
rows.anchor: لأن من طلب منه الهداية ونسب الإنعام إليه لا يناسبه نسبة الغضب إليه

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Blessing is good and favor, while anger is retribution; God names the more complete and prior quality and leaves the contrasting agent unstated, as elsewhere in the Quran.
rows.anchor: أن النعمةَ هي الخير والفضل، والغضب من باب الانتقام

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: God alone is the source of blessing, while angels, prophets, messengers, and allies also share anger at His enemies; the passive wording signals this.
rows.anchor: إن الله سبحانه هو المتفرد بالنعم

rows.speaker: التفسير القيم
rows.claim: Omitting the agent of anger belittles its targets, while naming the giver of blessing honors the recipients.
rows.anchor: إن في حذف فاعل الغضب من الإشعار بإهانة المغضوب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal forms make anger and misguidance fixed conditions that persist in this world and the next, unlike temporary verb forms.
rows.anchor: المغضوب عليهم والضالين اسماً، وذلك للدلالة على الثبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding lā before the astray makes the exclusion apply to either group separately, rather than only excluding people who combine anger and misguidance.
rows.anchor: لئلا يفهم أن المباينة لمن جمع الغضب والضلال دون من لم يجمعهما

rows.speaker: حاشية الجرجاني على الكشاف
rows.claim: In negation, the added lā after the coordinating conjunction explicitly attaches negation to each item and prevents reading only the combined pair as negated.
rows.anchor: أن (لا) المسماة بالمزيدة عند البصريين، إنما تقع بعد الواو العاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s order prompts the question why the angry are named before the astray.
rows.anchor: وقد تقول: ولمَ قدّم الغضبَ على الضلال، فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowing rebel is more culpable than the ignorant because knowledge followed by denial brings a graver sin and punishment.
rows.anchor: أن المغضوب عليه أشد ضلالاً وجرماً وعقوبة لأنه علم وجحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound hadith identifies the angry as Jews and the astray as Christians; the Jews came earlier, fitting their precedence in the verse.
rows.anchor: جاء في الحديث الصحيح أن المغضوب عليهم اليهود والضالين النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowing disobedience of Iblis was the first sin; after it, he vowed to mislead humanity, so anger appropriately precedes misguidance.
rows.anchor: وهي معصية إبليس، ذلك أنه كان عالماً بالحق عارفاً له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first sin on earth was Cain’s deliberate killing of his brother after their offerings, another case of wrongdoing by a knowing person.
rows.anchor: وهي قتل ابن آدم أخاه، بعد أن قَرَّبا قرباناً،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angry contrast directly with the recipients of blessing, as one may say a ruler blessed one person and was angered by another, unlike the unrelated verb strayed.
rows.anchor: فلان أنعم عليه الخليفة، وفلان غضب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After praising God and declaring worship and reliance, a person who strays is among those angry upon, so distance from that group is requested first.
rows.anchor: إذا زاغ كان من المغضوب عليهم، لأنه علم وخالف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After asking for guidance, it is fitting to ask distance from misguidance; this order also suits the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وأما سؤال الهداية بعد ذلك وهو قوله:

rows.speaker: البحر المحيط
rows.claim: Although anger results from misguidance, anger is placed beside blessing because blessing and retribution correspond semantically; the final wording also suits the rhyme.
rows.anchor: وقدم الغضب على الضلال، وإن كان الغضب من نتيجة الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unrestricted praise and the enduring nominal descriptions of the angry and astray all suggest timeless, lasting states.
rows.anchor: أن الحمد مطلق غير مقيد بزمن ولا بفاعل معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who fails to praise God, recognize Him as Lord, or receive the mercy of the Most Merciful is angry upon and astray.
rows.anchor: أنَّ مَنْ لم يحمد الله، فهو مغضوب عليه وضال،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Failure to believe in the Day of Judgment and God’s ownership of it makes a person angry upon and astray.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يؤمن بيوم الدين، وأن الله مالك ذلك اليوم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who does not devote worship and reliance to God alone, or follow the straight path of the blessed, is angry upon and astray.
rows.anchor: ومَنْ لم يَخُصَّ اللهَ بالعبادة والاستعانة، فهو مغضوبٌ عليه وضال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah gathers the foundations of Islamic belief: God and His perfect attributes, monotheism, the Last Day, divine power, and the messengers and revelation.
rows.anchor: إن هذه السورة جمعت أصول العقيدة الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s lordship over all entails that He alone is Lord, while exclusive worship and reliance affirm that there is no deity but Him.
rows.anchor: فإن كونه رباً للعالمين جميعاً، يعني: أنه لا رَبَّ سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God master of the Day of Judgment affirms the afterlife and recompense.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {مالك يَوْمِ الدين} يعني: الإقرار باليوم الآخر والجزاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking aid from God affirms His unlimited power.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} يعني: الإقرار بقدرته التي لا تُحَدُّ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is known through prophets and messengers; acceptable worship comes from revelation, not from each person’s preference.
rows.anchor: فإن الصراط المستقيم الذي يريده الله إنما يعرف من طريق الأنبياء والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah contains the religion’s two pillars, faith and righteous action; the faith section names belief in God, His messengers, and the Last Day.
rows.anchor: وتضمنت دين الإسلام بركنيه، الإيمان والعمل الصالح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Righteous action appears in worship and seeking aid through the end of the surah.
rows.anchor: وأما العمل الصالح فقد دخل في قوله: {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ}

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Praise of God implies that a Creator exists, knows, has power, and deserves praise and glorification.
rows.anchor: فقوله {الحمد للَّهِ} يدل على وجود الصانع، وعلى علمه وقدرته

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Lord of all worlds establishes God’s oneness and ownership of all creation, with no other lord or deity.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله: {رَبِّ العالمين} فهو يدل على أن ذلك الإله واحد

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The Merciful and Compassionate names express the one God’s complete mercy, generosity, favor, and beneficence.
rows.anchor: أما قوله: {الرحمان الرحيم} فيدل على أن الإله الواحد

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: God’s mastery of Judgment Day entails resurrection for distinguishing good from evil and vindicating the oppressed; without it, divine mercy would be impugned.
rows.anchor: أن يحصل بعد هذا اليوم، يومٌ آخر يظهر فيه تمييز المحسن عن المسيء،

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi summarizes praise as God’s existence and choice, lordship as unity, mercy as compassion in both worlds, and Judgment Day as wisdom and mercy.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {الرحمان الرحيم} يدل على رحمته في الدنيا والآخرة.

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The servant’s deeds require worship and recognition that he cannot perform it without God’s aid.
rows.anchor: أما الأعمال التي يأتي بها العبد فلها ركنان

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The surah is truly the Mother of the Book because it contains both doctrinal foundations and the two pillars of action.
rows.anchor: فهذه السورة هي أم الكتاب حقاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author first connected the Meccan oath to the Prophet’s hardship while preaching there: humans are created amid struggle, a message meant to console and strengthen him.
rows.anchor: أقسم بمكة حالَ كونِ الرسول فيها والرسول كان يلاقي فيها عنتاً ومشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s link to al-Fajr is its description of people who mistake wealth or restricted provision for honor or humiliation, followed by their neglect of orphans and the poor and greed for wealth.
rows.anchor: إن مناسبة هذه السورة لما قبلها - أعني سورة الفجر - قوله تعالى:
